A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original covariance-error and sampling experiments on synthetic data, plus OCM image-generation results measured using FID, NLL, and recall in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original OCM experiments and adds a forty-Gaussian demonstration, ground-truth covariance comparisons, and a Rademacher-sample ablation.

M1.justification: The OCM objective, shared pretrained score network and diagonal-Hessian prediction head, and DDPM/DDIM sampling procedures remain unchanged. Full-covariance sampling appears as an experimental comparator, not a new component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds a two-dimensional forty-Gaussian distribution with randomly located means and broader components in Section 5.1. The original nine-Gaussian grid remains in Appendix C.1, and the image datasets are retained. This is a limited extension of synthetic-data coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds samplers using true diagonal and full covariance to the retained nine-Gaussian DDPM/DDIM comparisons, matching v2 Figure 3 to v3 Figure 4. These comparators also appear in the new Figure 1. The image-benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new CIFAR10 cosine-schedule ablation evaluates training-time Rademacher sample counts M = 1, 3, 5, and 10 at 10, 25, 50, and 100 sampling steps. The new forty-Gaussian sampling experiment uses true scores. The retained image-training and evaluation protocols in Appendix B.2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted comparisons of full versus diagonal covariance and an ablation testing sensitivity to the Rademacher sample count during OCM training. The latter differs from v2's existing visualization of direct Rademacher covariance estimation. The original true-score versus learned-score covariance-error analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard deviations in Table 9 and specify three evaluations with different seeds, in v2 Appendix C.2 and v3 Appendix C.4. No new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing procedure accompanies the added experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds forty-Gaussian MMD results, ground-truth covariance curves, and Table 11's ablation results. For example, at 10 sampling steps, FID is 14.32 for M = 1 and 14.16 for M = 10, with NLL 4.99 for both; these compare different settings, not version-level performance gains. The retained nine-Gaussian plots omit their former one-step results. Existing image-benchmark table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The three theorems and their Appendix A proofs retain the same mathematical substance. Theorem 2 now explicitly identifies the base objective as Equation (10) with M tending to infinity, which was already explained in v2 Appendix A.2. Other equation changes are equivalent formatting or renumbering.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unbiased learning of diagonal denoising covariance from learned scores and improvements in sampling efficiency, generation quality, diversity, and likelihood. Adding 'Diagonal' to the title and revising the abstract clarify the existing focus without materially changing the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explains why full covariance helps on the forty-Gaussian example but offers little benefit on the symmetric nine-Gaussian example. Section 6 discusses low-rank or block-diagonal alternatives and additional applications. Appendix C.3 attributes small benefits from larger M to reduced gradient-estimation variance.

D1.justification: Section 3 clarifies that each Hessian-vector calculation requires a forward pass and backward propagation, refining v2's description of two network passes. Tables 6 and 7 correct the ImageNet resolution typo from 256x156 to 256x256. Architectures, training budgets, hardware, sampling details, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds references and discussion covering distributional, latent-variable, and energy-based reverse models, inverse problems, and general differential-equation samplers. Examples include Bortoli et al. (2025), Yu et al. (2024), Xu et al. (2024), and Rozet et al. (2024). The central positioning relative to covariance-estimation methods is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and terminology edits, clarifies Theorem 2, updates the title and publication header, and revises acknowledgments. It moves the original toy discussion to Appendix C.1 and expands the future-directions discussion, while retaining the overall document structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds the forty-Gaussian Figure 1 and ablation Table 11, while Figure 2 redisplays existing FID/NLL results. It updates toy-plot legends and ranges, moves earlier figures into the appendix, and corrects Table 10's dataset caption. Most tables and sample grids retain their presentation. The new Table 11 incorrectly labels NLL as a percentage with an upward arrow.

improvement.justification: The added covariance comparators clarify the limits of diagonal modeling, and Table 11 provides empirical support for the previously asserted adequacy of M = 1. These additions modestly strengthen the paper's evidence and interpretation while preserving its method and main benchmark results. The gains are limited by missing uncertainty estimates for the small ablation differences and minor presentation errors, including Table 11's NLL label.
